questions.question: What is the official source for a *market* price to measure our own line against?
questions.known: Official league sources publish results, stats and schedules, but not betting prices. Sportsbook prices are commercial data.

questions.current_answer: No official league source publishes betting prices; the board records this as GAP-01 and leaves market cells blank with the reason (model_lines.tsv market_status; F18). Market values that do appear come from a third-party feed and are labelled per row (market_provenance in data/fair_lines.csv). The open half is approval of a market-price source for headline numbers (Q21, Q30, Q32; D-20).

questions.question: What sample size would make a strategy's result distinguishable from luck, and how long is one NFL season?
questions.known: A 2026 regular season runs 18 weeks; Week 10 is in progress and the league calendar shows Week 18 on Jan 9-10, 2027, with Super Bowl LXI on Feb 14, 2027 (S05). Division standings confirm clubs have played 8-9 games (S02).
questions.unknown: The effect size any strategy will actually achieve, which is what determines the sample needed.
questions.missing_information: Historical graded results to estimate variance.
questions.recommended_path: State a minimum sample gate up front, pre-register it, and refuse to rank a strategy until it clears the gate. Use a binomial or bootstrap interval, not a bare win rate.
questions.current_answer: Answered per strategy by the removal-of-luck panels: skill means the 95% lower bound of hit rate clears the vig-adjusted break-even hurdle after a multiplicity adjustment for every trial run (the register's best ROI entry is rejected on exactly this: 936 settled bets, 51.07% lower bound vs 52.38% hurdle — data/luck_panel_signal.json). The open half: which number becomes the leaderboard's standing qualification bar (Q43).

options.label: Recommended path
